meta.title: Risk Monitor
meta.window_note: Each strip's marker is the current value's percentile over the indicator's full available history, oriented so rightward = riskier. The ghost marker is the value ~one month earlier (prior quarter for quarterly series). Strips with under 10 years of history are flagged.
meta.phase_note: Automatable core — 15 FRED gauges plus register and The Read. Still to come: scrape/paid gauges (Shiller CAPE & equity risk premium, FDIC bank capital, CFTC basis-trade short) and the monthly PDF email.

regime.quadrant_label: Building — calm markets, elevated vulnerability (the dangerous cell)

whats_changed.text: Sahm rule (real-time) moved 21 percentile points less risky (now 33th).
5y5y forward inflation breakeven moved 6 percentile points riskier (now 57th).
↑ Register: Disorderly fiscal repricing — rising (10-20% over 12m).
↑ Register: Tariff-driven inflation resurgence — rising (20-35% over 12m).
↓ Register: Commercial real-estate credit strain — easing (15-30% over 12m).
↑ Register: Geopolitical oil shock — rising (15-25% over 12m).

read.lead: The setup is the dangerous one
read.body: Markets are calm while the balance sheet is stretched — stress sits near its 40th historical percentile, vulnerability near its 80th. That low-stress / high-vulnerability combination is the "building" regime: the quiet stretch in which leverage and valuations accumulate, and in which a shock does the most damage precisely because nobody is positioned for it.

read.lead: Where the fragility lives is valuation and leverage, not households
read.body: Equity market cap is near 218% of GDP and home prices are rich relative to rents, while corporate leverage and the federal interest burden keep climbing. The reassuring counterpoint is the household sector: debt-to-GDP is near its lowest in decades and debt-service is contained. The vulnerability is concentrated in asset prices and in corporate and public balance sheets, not on kitchen tables.

read.lead: The one live wire this month is oil
read.body: Oil volatility has spiked from the low 40s to near 60 in a matter of days — the single gauge flashing in the fast panel — a reminder that the geopolitical tail is not priced. Credit spreads, equity vol, and funding markets are otherwise benign, which is exactly what makes a sudden repricing possible.

The tells for the top risks are all on the page: the yield-curve slope and the federal interest burden for a fiscal repricing, the SOFR–IORB spread for a funding-driven basis-trade unwind, and 5y5y breakevens for tariff-driven inflation. None is sounding an alarm today; the point of the monitor is to catch the one that moves first.

risks.name: Disorderly fiscal repricing
risks.blurb: A buyers'-strike moment at a Treasury auction — term premium jumps, the long end sells off, and it feeds into mortgages and credit. Interest is already ~21% of federal receipts and rising.

risks.name: Leveraged Treasury basis-trade unwind
risks.blurb: Hedge funds run a large, highly levered long-cash / short-futures Treasury trade. A funding shock or margin spike could force a fire-sale into thin liquidity, echoing March 2020.

risks.name: Tariff-driven inflation resurgence
risks.blurb: Tariff pass-through and supply frictions push core goods prices back up, un-anchoring expectations and boxing in the Fed. Breakevens are the tell.

risks.name: AI-led equity air-pocket
risks.blurb: Equity market cap sits near 218% of GDP, concentrated in a handful of AI names. A growth or capex disappointment could trigger a sharp, concentration-amplified drawdown.

risks.name: Commercial real-estate credit strain
risks.blurb: Office and multifamily refinancing at higher rates pressures regional-bank balance sheets. Slow-burn rather than acute, and easing at the margin.

risks.name: Geopolitical oil shock
risks.blurb: An escalation that disrupts supply spikes crude and oil volatility, a stagflationary impulse. Oil-vol (OVX) has already jumped this month.

panels.title: Stress
panels.subtitle: How scared is everyone right now

strips.label: Yield-curve slope (10y − 3m)
strips.note: Treasury term spread; a negative (inverted) curve has preceded every modern recession, so a lower value is riskier.

strips.label: Sahm rule (real-time)
strips.note: Rise in the unemployment rate off its recent low; 0.50pp has historically marked the start of a recession.

strips.label: Initial jobless claims (4-wk avg)
strips.note: Four-week moving average of first-time unemployment claims — the fastest read on layoffs.

strips.label: 5y5y forward inflation breakeven
strips.note: Market-implied inflation over the five years starting five years out — the cleanest read on unanchored expectations.

strips.label: Equity volatility (VIX)
strips.note: S&P 500 30-day implied volatility — the classic fear gauge.

strips.label: Corporate credit spread (Baa − 10y)
strips.note: Moody's Baa corporate yield over the 10-year Treasury; widens when investors demand more to hold credit risk. (FRED's ICE high-yield OAS is license-truncated to ~3 years, so this deep-history spread is used.)

strips.label: Financial conditions (NFCI)
strips.note: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index; 0 is average, positive is tighter-than-average conditions.

strips.label: Oil volatility (OVX)
strips.note: CBOE crude-oil implied volatility — a proxy for energy / geopolitical stress.

panels.title: Vulnerabilities
panels.subtitle: How much damage a shock would do

strips.label: Home price-to-rent
strips.note: Case-Shiller home prices relative to CPI rent, both indexed to the start of the sample; high means housing is dear versus rents.

strips.label: Equity market cap / GDP
strips.note: Market value of nonfinancial corporate equities as a share of GDP (a Buffett-style gauge); high means richly valued stocks.

strips.label: Household debt-service ratio
strips.note: Required debt payments as a share of disposable income — how stretched household cash flow is.

strips.label: Household debt / GDP
strips.note: Total household debt relative to the size of the economy (BIS).

strips.label: Nonfinancial corporate debt / GDP
strips.note: Debt securities and loans of nonfinancial corporations as a share of GDP — corporate leverage across the cycle.

strips.label: SOFR − IORB spread
strips.note: Secured overnight funding rate minus interest on reserves; a positive, widening spread signals scarce cash in money markets.

strips.label: Federal interest / receipts
strips.note: Federal interest payments as a share of federal receipts — how much of revenue is pre-committed to servicing the debt.
